In [[mathematics]], the '''qualitative theory of differential equations''' studies the behavior of [[differential equation]]s by means other than finding their solutions. It originated from the works of [[Henri Poincaré]] and [[Aleksandr Lyapunov]]. There are relatively few differential equations that can be solved explicitly, but using tools from [[mathematical analysis|analysis]] and [[topology]], one can "solve" them in the qualitative sense, obtaining information about their properties.<ref>{{springer|title=Qualitative theory of differential equations|id=Qualitative_theory_of_differential_equations}}</ref>

It was used by [[Benjamin Kuipers]] in the book ''Qualitative reasoning: modeling and simulation with incomplete knowledge'' to demonstrate how the theory of [[Partial differential equation|PDEs]] can be applied even in situations where only qualitative knowledge is available.
